title: Keep the train registry and per-train documents mutually coherent

facts.note: The check is a corpus-wide invariant evaluated at CONFIRM (confirm-blocking) regardless of what the plan changed; the harness must report the phase.
The registry file and the per-train document directory are the artifacts compared; they are read whole-corpus at CONFIRM, not only when touched by the diff.

Needs a corpus-level detector: every registry row path must resolve to a file anywhere on disk (dangling direction); every non-underscore per-train document under plan/_trains must be named by a row (orphan direction). Pre-existing violations count, independent of the current change.

fires: At CONFIRM, any plan/_trains.yaml row names a path that does not resolve to a file, wherever that path points.
At CONFIRM, a per-train document under plan/_trains (not underscore-prefixed) is named by no registry row.
A dangling row or orphan document already existed before this plan, and the plan only edits unrelated content: confirmation still checks and reports it.
A plan adds, renames, moves or removes a train row or document without updating the other side.
doesNotFire: Orphan direction only: underscore-prefixed sidecars under plan/_trains (_aliases.yaml, the _interlockings subtree) are not enumerated as per-train documents needing a row; a registry row naming a missing sidecar path is still a dangling row.
A content-only edit to a train document when every row resolves and every document is registered (the corpus is coherent in both directions).
Coherence inside the _interlockings subtree, which is governed by its own rules.

given: At CONFIRM, the corpus contains plan/_trains.yaml and per-train documents under plan/_trains, whatever this plan changed.
then: Every registry row must name a path that resolves to an existing file, and every non-underscore per-train document under plan/_trains must be named by a row: no dangling rows, no orphans.
prefer: Plan a train's registry row and document as one change, both derived from its train_id.
Remove a train's row and document together.
Fix pre-existing dangling rows or orphans before confirming.
avoid: Writing a row before its document exists (dangling row): consumers resolve through it and some crash.
Leaving a document no row names (orphan): inert, but residue of document-before-registry ordering.
Counting underscore sidecars as per-train documents.
Repointing planner.train.registry's validator ref; the conventions sweep owns it.
unless: Underscore-prefixed sidecars under plan/_trains (_aliases.yaml, _interlockings/) are not per-train documents, so they need no registry row.
why: Consumers resolve trains through the registry, so a row naming an absent file breaks them; unregistered documents are residue of document-before-registry ordering and must be reportable.
evidence: Each failure reports train_id, direction (dangling or orphan), registry_value and document_value.
verifier_detail: Direction 1 (dangling_row): for each entry in plan/_trains.yaml, the named path must resolve to a file on disk; the target location is not restricted to plan/_trains and no sidecar exclusion applies to this direction.
Direction 2 (orphan_document): each per-train document under plan/_trains must be named by some registry row.

Registry sidecars: underscore-prefixed names under plan/_trains (_aliases.yaml, _interlockings subtree) are excluded from Direction 2 enumeration only; _interlockings coherence is checked by planner.interlocking.registry-mirrors-document and planner.train.interlocking-home.

Validation: family=coherence, template=cross_artifact_existence_agreement, variant=planner_train_registry_existence, phase=CONFIRM, enforcement=confirm-blocking, subject_kind=train. Evaluated over the whole corpus, not only diff-touched rows.
failure_evidence fields: train_id, direction, registry_value, document_value.

test_route_space_admission dies on a dangling row with a bare FileNotFoundError rather than reporting it; every consumer walking the registry resolves through rows; this validator reports dangling rows instead.
Orphans are inert (nothing resolves through them) but must be reportable, otherwise create_train's document-before-registry ordering is unsupported.
audit: Source name: 'The train registry and the documents it indexes both exist'.

Dangling rows were the residue create_train left when it wrote the registry before the document (#1942); create_train now uses document-before-registry ordering, which deliberately leaves orphans, so orphans must be reportable or that choice is unsupported.

Why a NEW node rather than a validator hung on planner.train.registry: that node already claims at disposition strict that "every registry entry MUST have a corresponding spec file" (the dangling direction of this rule) but has never been able to enforce it. Its implementation.ref names the Y003 sweep's convention variant conventions/resolution/test_train_validation, which instantiates direct_reference_resolution and checks that a train's participant references resolve to existing wagons; it never reads a path. The reverse-coherence binder (coach/validators/test_rule_validator_binding.py) exempts convention-variant refs from the bind_rule callsite requirement, so the gap drew no complaint.

Repointing planner.train.registry here was the first attempt and is wrong: the Y003 guard (validators/conventions/tests/test_y003_sweep_coverage_guards.py, SWEPT_RULE_TO_VARIANT) deliberately pins planner.train.registry to a conventions/ variant, so the ref is an architectural decision owned by the sweep, not an oversight to undo from here.

So the claim is enforced under its own id; closing the gap on planner.train.registry (giving its swept variant a real path-existence check, or folding that node into this one) stays with the conventions-sweep owners.

sharedNodes.text: strict: fails on every finding, no advisory mode, no ratchet baseline.

additions.text: Plan row and document as one change derived from train_id; remove both together; fix pre-existing violations before confirming.
additions.justification: Concrete planner moves implied by the bidirectional CONFIRM-blocking invariant and the graph edge to planner.train.naming (paths derive from train_id).

additions.text: fires/doesNotFire scenarios, including pre-existing violations and the content-only coherent case.
additions.justification: Required by schema; derived from statement, terms, sidecar definition and CONFIRM phase.
Makes explicit that the source invariant is unconditional at CONFIRM, not tied to a train lifecycle change.
